answer: The paper's ITL formula ITL = alpha/(1 - lambda*W/N_D) holds in BLIS with excellent accuracy (<1% error) at rates 1-50 req/s where the system reaches steady state. With sufficient requests for convergence (3000), it extends to <4% error for AD and <7% for AL up to rate=100. The formula breaks down for AL above rate ~130 (14.5% error at 150) because BLIS's max_num_running_reqs=256 caps the batch size, causing ITL to grow linearly instead of as 1/(1-rho). AD is unaffected within [1,150] because its lower per-request work keeps batches below the cap. The paper's qualitative predictions are fully confirmed: ITL_AD < ITL_AL at all rates >1 (0-8.7% reduction), and TTFT_AD > TTFT_AL at all rates (4-16ms overhead). With the prescribed 300 requests, an apparent formula breakdown at high rates is actually a transient measurement artifact — the simulation doesn't reach steady state at rate >50.
